name: Cefazolin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 500 mg to 1 g IV every 6 to 8 hours
1 to 2 g (3 g if 120 kg or more) 30 to 60 minutes before incision; 500 mg to 1 g during long surgery and every 6 to 8 hours for 24 hours after
35–54: usual dose every 8 hours or longer; 11–34: half dose every 12 hours; 10 or less: half dose every 18 to 24 hours

key_interactions.effect: Blocks tubular secretion; higher and longer drug levels (label).

serious: Anaphylaxis and serious hypersensitivity (cross-reactivity with penicillins up to 10%)
Seizures in kidney impairment when doses are not reduced

contraindications: Immediate hypersensitivity to cefazolin, cephalosporins, penicillins or other beta-lactams
monitoring: Prothrombin time in patients at risk
Signs of seizures in kidney impairment

pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 60% in 6 hours and 70% to 80% in 24 hours, unchanged in urine
